newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Data on Brazil property lacking -- and so is rent.
newsitem.headline: Data on Brazil property lacking -- and so is rent.

text.p: The Brazilian government is losing out on $1.7 billion a year in rent because it does not know how many or even which properties it owns, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.

Helio Gehrke, the man charged with looking after the government's diverse apartments, beaches, islands and buildings, told reporters the ministry was carrying out a study to identify its properties but would not complete it until 2002.
Gehrke said he had identified 3 million state-owned properties so far, of which rent was being collected on 500,000.
"There are people who don't even know their apartments or land is owned by the government. And even the government isn't aware that it is the owner," he said.
This year the government hopes to earn $280 million in rent. But Gehrke acknowledged it should be raking in about $2 billion a year.
A local newspaper reported on Monday that the five-star Sheraton hotel in Rio de Janeiro was built on government land.
Gehrke said he did not know if it was. "We shall have to check it out," he said.
